sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Floirac, a commune on the right bank of the Garonne in Gironde, takes its main parking rules from Bordeaux Métropole and its own measures are small. Since 1 January 2025 the Métropole's low-emission zone has covered everything inside the ring road, barring only unclassified vehicles [0]; unclassified vehicles may still reach 11 park-and-ride sites by dedicated access roads, two of which are in Floirac, Parc Relais Arena and Parc Relais Dravemont [1]. The town's centre-bourg car park on rue Jules Guesde is a blue zone with 27 places and a 90-minute free stay on weekdays, monitored by sensors linked to the municipal police [2]. On public roads municipal and national police handle abusive parking [3]. Floirac became a 30 km/h town in 2023 [4].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The pressure point is the Arkéa Arena. For events the town urges spectators to use public transport, bike or car-sharing, and to park at TBM park-and-ride sites linked to the special shuttle; anti-parking bollards have been installed and the municipal police fine and impound vehicles blocking pavements, bus stops or business entrances [5]. A September 2024 TBM leaflet said an Arena shuttle ran on show days from Stalingrad and Gare Saint-Jean every 5 to 10 minutes, and the 2026 accessibility guide gives every 6 to 15 minutes [13]. The Arena's own multi-storey car park, run by Metpark, has close to 1,000 places including more than 20 for two-wheelers, and a space can be bought with a show ticket [6]; 22 are for reduced-mobility visitors who can book up to 48 hours before an event [7]. The park-and-ride ticket for the Arena was 4.50 euros in 2024 [12]. For charging, the national database lists at Floirac addresses six 180 kW points on rue de la Gabarre, in service since November 2024, and a Lidl site with eight points; it is filled in by operators and may be incomplete [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Metpark describes itself as a public industrial and commercial body for Bordeaux and its metropolis, governed by a board of 11 Métropole elected members, and says it plans 1,500 charge points in 26 car parks by 2026 [8]. TBM, run by Keolis for the Métropole, lists Dravemont as season-ticket holders only with 46 spaces [9], yet also among the 11 sites selling two-to-five-day tickets at 12 to 25 euros, which sits oddly with that listing [11]. TBM's pages give a 15-euro fine for using a park-and-ride outside tram hours [10]; other TBM pages give a different amount, so we do not rely on it.

Our data cover two car parks. The Floirac Arena park-and-ride (962 spaces in the feed, against 'close to 1,000' for the Metpark car park) was measured since 24 September 2026 and averaged about 22% on weekdays and 13% at weekends, with a reading at full on a Monday evening at about 21:00, consistent with event traffic. Dravemont (41 spaces in the feed against 46 listed) has only about ten days of readings, since 12 October, and averaged 17% on weekdays. About four weeks of data, not covering a full event season.
